## Tour through San Agustín de Callo: a historic stop near Cotopaxi

[Hacienda San Agustín de Callo](/ecuador/place/san-agustin-de-callo/) is situated near Lasso in the Ecuadorian Andes. It is distinctive for preserved sections of an Inca structure, Spanish colonial architecture and later buildings within a working estate. Its history comes alive through the actual stone walls and courtyard.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring a scheduled visit here. Our itinerary is ["Ecuador: Wildlife of the Andes and Amazon in 15 Days"](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/). This page explains the hacienda's place in a longer journey so that a sightseeing stop is not confused with accommodation at the historic hotel.

## On which day is the visit scheduled?

San Agustín de Callo appears on **day 9** of the itinerary, when travellers leave the Quito region for Cotopaxi. The route crosses a high-altitude section of the Andes often called the Avenue of the Volcanoes. Exploring the historic estate adds a cultural element to a day framed by volcanic scenery.

The visit includes touring the hacienda, opportunities to feed llamas and take photographs, and time for lunch. **Lunch is not included in the price for this day.** Afterwards, travellers continue to **La Cienega** hotel for the night. The tour does not include an overnight stay at San Agustín de Callo itself.

The following day is devoted to Cotopaxi National Park and the return to Quito. Choosing this route solely for the hacienda makes sense only if the wider programme also appeals: highland landscapes, nature walks and the journey onwards into the Amazon.

## What makes the hacienda visit special?

Historical accounts of San Agustín de Callo describe an architectural combination of three periods: Inca, Spanish colonial and republican. The old stone blocks display distinctive precision fitting, while adjacent courtyard sections reflect other building traditions. Seeing these together is especially interesting after visiting Quito's urban monuments.

This is a functioning historic estate, not an archaeological park with unrestricted access. Entry to particular rooms, dining or an overnight stay depends on arrangements with the property. Even if the hacienda itself offers these services, **they are not necessarily included in the Ada Tours itinerary**.

Travellers particularly interested in history can also explore [Ecuador culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/). On this journey, the historic stop complements a nature-focused route.

## Why visit the hacienda together with Cotopaxi?

The estate is on a high-altitude plateau close to the volcano. In clear weather, the snow-covered summit of Cotopaxi may be visible from open areas. This location makes it possible to combine historic architecture with the volcanic landscapes explored later.

On the [15-day programme](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/), a national park excursion follows the historic day; [Limpiopungo Lake](/ecuador/place/limpiopungo-lake/) is also listed among the route's sites. Highland walking and leisurely exploration of the hacienda's courtyard require different preparation. In the park, altitude, wind and physical wellbeing matter; at the estate, it is chiefly a question of allowing sufficient time.

If you are sensitive to altitude, discuss the pace of mountain stops and any limitations on that particular day with Ada Tours beforehand. Distance from Quito alone is a poor guide to this part of the journey: elevation changes and weather greatly affect how travellers feel.

## What to check before choosing

**Type of stop.** San Agustín de Callo is part of the sightseeing itinerary, but accommodation and a separate extended programme on its grounds are not advertised for this tour.

**Meals.** Time is set aside for lunch on the day of the visit, but it is paid for separately. The overnight stay is at La Cienega.

**Continuing the journey.** After Cotopaxi, the itinerary visits other natural regions and includes [Sacha Reserve](/ecuador/place/sacha-reserve/) in the Amazon. Pack for both cool Andean conditions and humid rainforest. To compare the full range of trips, see our [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the tour through San Agustín de Callo

### Can you stay overnight at San Agustín de Callo itself?

The hacienda offers accommodation, but on this tour the overnight stay is at La Cienega. A different arrangement would need to be agreed individually.

### Is lunch included on the day of the visit?

No. The published programme explicitly states that lunch on day 9 is not included.

### Is this a separate excursion or part of a larger tour?

In our current selection, the hacienda visit is part of the [15-day Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/), which also includes nature and city stops.

### What follows the hacienda visit?

Cotopaxi National Park is scheduled for the next day, and the journey then continues towards other parts of Ecuador and the Amazon.

  San Cristóbal is a Galápagos island with sea lions near Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, nature trails, the freshwater El Junco Lagoon and the offshore rock formations of León Dormido. Discover how to combine coastal walks with boat excursions and how the island differs from Santa Cruz.

## San Cristóbal Island in the Galápagos: sea lions, León Dormido and El Junco Lagoon

San Cristóbal belongs to Ecuador's [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). It is home to Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, the administrative capital of Galápagos Province. One of the island's attractions is that you can encounter wildlife close to the town, while entirely different landscapes appear as you head farther inland.

The island's main experiences fall into three groups: sea lions and birds along the coast, boat trips to offshore volcanic rocks, and humid green highlands with a freshwater lagoon. Each takes a different amount of time and preparation, so it is best to plan your stay around specific activities.

## Puerto Baquerizo Moreno and the sea lions on the coast

Puerto Baquerizo Moreno's waterfront, beaches and rocky shorelines are known for sea lions. You may see them resting on the sand or returning from the water. They are interesting to watch without taking a long boat trip: the animals use the urban shoreline as part of their natural habitat.

Being accustomed to people does not make sea lions tame. Do not approach a resting animal for a photograph, block its way to the water or attempt to touch a pup. Choose a viewing spot and allow the animals to move freely.

La Lobería and Punta Carola beaches lie near the town. They are suitable for discovering the coast, while swimming depends on sea conditions and instructions from local authorities. Animals may occupy parts of a beach, so choose where to rest in accordance with conservation restrictions.

## Tijeretas and the history of the Galápagos Islands

Near Puerto Baquerizo Moreno is an interpretation centre explaining the archipelago's volcanic origins, settlement, ecosystems and conservation challenges. From here, a trail leads to Tijeretas, a hill with viewpoints above the ocean.

Two species of frigatebirds can be observed in the same colony in this area, making it an interesting place to compare them closely. Bring water, sun protection and shoes suitable for rocky ground.

Allow dedicated time for Tijeretas rather than treating it as an incidental stop on the way to the beach. The trail combines wildlife observation, open views and an account of how people settled the islands.

## León Dormido: a sea excursion to the rocks

León Dormido, also called Kicker Rock, consists of sea stacks off San Cristóbal. Two towering rock masses are separated by a narrow passage through the water. From a boat, you can see the sheer walls and seabirds, while water excursions offer encounters with marine life around the rocks.

It is important to distinguish **sightseeing by boat**, **snorkelling with a mask** and **scuba diving**. These activities have different skill and health requirements. Even if promotional material mentions marine animals, meeting a particular species cannot be guaranteed.

Ocean currents, swell and underwater visibility vary. Route availability, guiding and included equipment depend on the operator and specific excursion. If you are primarily interested in underwater wildlife, compare actual programmes and participant requirements, not just pictures of the rocks.

## El Junco: freshwater in a volcanic crater

In the island's highlands lies [El Junco Lagoon](/ecuador/place/el-junco-lagoon/). It is a freshwater body inside the crater of an extinct volcano, filled mainly by rainfall. Unlike the dry coastal stretches, its surroundings feature green slopes and moist vegetation.

Frigatebirds and other birds can be seen above the lagoon. Highland weather differs from the coast: clouds, wind and rain may change the conditions even within a day. Walking requires footwear with good grip, as the ground can become slippery after rain.

El Junco presents a side of the Galápagos that contrasts with the usual image of black lava and ocean surf: a green volcanic basin holding freshwater. A trip into the island's interior therefore complements rather than repeats the sea excursion.

## How to divide your time on San Cristóbal

For a short introduction, choose one main activity and add a coastal walk. Trying to combine a distant boat excursion, a highland trip and a long coastal trail in a single day is risky: boat activities depend on weather, and overland travel takes time.

| Type of day | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Town and coast | Sea lions, beaches |
| Nature trail | Tijeretas, frigatebirds |
| Highlands | El Junco Lagoon |
| Sea excursion | León Dormido, ocean |

If the island is part of a cruise, the vessel's schedule limits the time available at each landing. When staying at a land-based hotel, you have more flexibility in choosing excursions, but boat trips still depend on weather and national park regulations.

## San Cristóbal or Santa Cruz: which to choose?

[Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) is known for Puerto Ayora, the [highlands with giant tortoises](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) and research centres. It makes a convenient base for land and sea programmes in the central archipelago.

San Cristóbal is particularly appealing for its sea lions near town, Tijeretas, freshwater lagoon and excursions to León Dormido. If wildlife viewing and contrasting natural zones on a single island are your priority, San Cristóbal offers several distinct experiences without necessarily travelling to neighbouring islands.

Moving between islands requires transport and coordinated schedules; it is not a short walk from one beach to another. When combining San Cristóbal with [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) or Santa Cruz, account for the order of flights, sea crossings and possible timetable changes.

## The island in Ada Tours programmes

On our [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the sea portion begins at San Cristóbal. After the flight and boarding the yacht, travellers head to El Junco Lagoon. The cruise then continues to other islands, including Floreana.

This is a confirmed example of visiting **El Junco specifically**, not a promise that the tour automatically includes every marine and coastal attraction on San Cristóbal. When choosing other itineraries, examine the precise island day and list of included activities.

Explore our [Ecuador tours catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) to compare journeys, or see [Ecuador nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) if you want to watch wildlife. Choose scuba diving separately among [diving programmes](/interests/diving/tours/ecuador/): snorkelling on a standard cruise is not a substitute for scuba diving.

## Frequently asked questions about San Cristóbal Island

### Can you see sea lions without a boat excursion?

Yes. On San Cristóbal, sea lions are often found on the waterfront at Puerto Baquerizo Moreno and nearby beaches. Keep your distance and follow conservation rules.

### Are León Dormido and Kicker Rock different places?

No. These are two names for the same rock formation off San Cristóbal. Visiting options may differ: a boat excursion, snorkelling or a separate diving trip.

### What makes El Junco Lagoon interesting?

It is a [freshwater lagoon](/ecuador/place/el-junco-lagoon/) in a volcanic crater, where you can experience moist highland landscapes and observe birds, including frigatebirds.

### Can you visit all the main sites in one day?

Usually it is better to choose a priority. Boat excursions and highland trips take time, and weather affects the schedule.

### Is diving essential to get to know the island?

No. Coastal wildlife viewing, a walk to Tijeretas and a trip to El Junco are all independent options. Diving requires a separate product with confirmed participant requirements.

## Tour through San Cristóbal: the first day of a Galápagos cruise

[San Cristóbal Island](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) is known for sea lions, coastal trails and nature routes through the green highlands. But when choosing a tour, it is important to distinguish the island's many attractions from the actual schedule of a particular programme.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with San Cristóbal on the main route. Ada Tours' confirmed product is the ["Ecuador and the Galápagos Islands with an 18-Day Cruise" itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/). Here San Cristóbal is the arrival point in the archipelago and the place where travellers board the yacht, while the day's principal excursion is to [El Junco Lagoon](/ecuador/place/el-junco-lagoon/).

## What is included on the island?

On **day 15**, participants have breakfast and a transfer before flying to the Galápagos Islands. After arrival and mandatory checks, the crew of **M/Y Grand Majestic** welcomes them and takes them aboard. The programme includes a standard cabin on a 5-star yacht, lunch and an introductory briefing about the cruise.

In the afternoon there is a visit to El Junco. This freshwater lagoon lies in a volcanic caldera in San Cristóbal's highlands. In contrast to the dry lava shores, the area has green slopes, humid air and habitats for waterbirds. Frigatebirds are explicitly mentioned in the itinerary, and the walk around the lagoon is described as easy to moderate.

Arrival day includes a flight, yacht embarkation and an excursion. It should not be treated as a free day for exploring the whole island independently. Any additional visits need to fit the yacht's departure time and the approved programme.

## How the four-day cruise continues

After San Cristóbal, the yacht's itinerary connects [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), [Española](/ecuador/place/espanola-island/) and [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The sea portion lasts **4 days and 3 nights**. Landings and nature activities follow the vessel's schedule; travellers move between islands aboard the yacht.

On the final day, a visit to Santa Cruz and a transfer to the airport on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) are scheduled for the return to the mainland. This is a continuous sea itinerary. The list of islands does not imply that travellers can freely choose how long to stay at each.

| Stage | Planned activity |
|---|---|
| San Cristóbal | Flight arrival, El Junco |
| Overnight stays | On the yacht |
| Next | Floreana and Española |
| Finish | Santa Cruz, Baltra |

To compare different sea-travel formats, explore [Ecuador cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/ecuador/). A land-based journey has different logistics: accommodation in a hotel on an island and separate day excursions rather than moving with the yacht.

## Which San Cristóbal attractions could be added separately?

Off the island's coast are the rock formations of León Dormido, or Kicker Rock. Two tall volcanic structures are separated by a narrow sea passage. According to Galápagos Conservancy, sea excursions here may allow wildlife viewing and snorkelling under suitable conditions.

**León Dormido is not listed as a visit on this 18-day tour.** The first island day's itinerary covers arrival, the yacht and El Junco. Likewise, La Lobería, Tijeretas and other popular attractions cannot be added automatically simply because they are on San Cristóbal. Learn more on the [island's own page](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/).

Diving may be another priority, but the word "cruise" does not itself guarantee scuba sessions. You need a separate product with clearly specified dives and participant requirements. Explore these among our [Ecuador diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/ecuador/).

## Preparing for a combined island and mainland journey

On this tour, travellers first discover the lowland Amazon, then the mountains and cloud forests of the Andes, and only afterwards fly to the Galápagos. Pack for rainy forest, cool highlands and sea excursions. Shoes for rocky shores and sun protection are useful alongside warm layers.

The island portion requires time for airport checks, boarding the yacht and complying with conservation rules. Fees, document requirements and restrictions on items brought into the islands may change, so check them for your travel dates. The [18-day tour description](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) lists included and extra expenses separately; they should not be assumed to apply to other cruises.

If seeing animals is your main aim, compare [Ecuador wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). On the islands, keeping the proper distance from sea lions and birds and staying on approved protected-area routes is as important as the opportunity to encounter them.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through San Cristóbal

### Can I spend several extra days on the island?

In the published itinerary, the island marks the beginning of a cruise. Separate accommodation and additional excursions on San Cristóbal would require agreement on a revised route.

### Is Kicker Rock included?

No. The particular programme specifies arrival, yacht accommodation and El Junco. An excursion to Kicker Rock is not among its included stops.

### Does the yacht include scuba diving?

A cruise alone does not establish that. For diving, choose a programme that explicitly lists dive sessions and participation requirements.

### How does San Cristóbal connect to the mainland journey?

It begins the final sea portion of the [18-day itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), preceded by the Andes and [Sacha Reserve](/ecuador/place/sacha-reserve/) in the Amazon.

## San Pablo Lake: Imbabura Volcano above the water

**San Pablo Lake (Lago San Pablo)** lies near [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/) in [Imbabura Province](/ecuador/place/imbabura-province/), northern Ecuador. Imbabura Volcano rises above the water, while rural communities and cultivated fields line the shores. The combination of lake, mountain and everyday Andean life makes San Pablo a convenient stop on the way from Quito.

Above all, this is **a lake with a view of the volcano**. A viewpoint stop, lakeside walk and boat ride are different experiences. Check which one is actually included in a tourism itinerary.

## Where is the lake and how can you see it?

San Pablo is in Otavalo Canton. The official Imbabura Geopark groups the lake and nearby [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/) within a regional geological and tourism route. Roads from Otavalo and neighbouring settlements reach the lake; the geopark identifies access through San Pablo and Araque.

San Pablo, Araque and other communities surround the water. You can see the volcanic landscape from different directions and watch Imbabura's broad slopes reflected in the lake.

### Miralago viewpoint

[Miralago](/ecuador/place/miralago/) is known for views over the lake and volcano. This stop works well when an excursion day has limited free time: a broad panorama is available without a long hike. Clouds may hide Imbabura's summit, so enjoy the wider landscape rather than counting on an unobstructed view of the peak.

## What to see beside the water

### Lakeside walks

Reed beds, fields and small settlements appear along the shores. San Pablo offers opportunities to walk in permitted areas and watch birds. Official regional materials also describe traditions of communities around the lake, including the use of aquatic plants in handicrafts.

Choose walking areas carefully: shores differ in accessibility and facilities. Private land and farmland are not public paths.

### Possible water activities

Imbabura Geopark mentions boat trips and recreational activities on the lake. However, these are **opportunities in the region**, not a guaranteed service on every sightseeing excursion. For a boat outing, check the operator, weather, safety equipment and whether it is included in your specific itinerary.

### Combining the lake with Otavalo's culture

Nearby you can explore Otavalo's craft traditions, visit market districts and see [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/). A nature stop at the lake complements excursions mainly focused on markets and local traditions.

## Planning an excursion from Quito

Journeys north from the capital commonly include Otavalo and the surrounding region. Allow time for driving, the market, viewpoints and any additional stops. Andean weather can change quickly, so a light jacket, rain protection and comfortable footwear are useful by the water.

Leave some flexibility when photographing the volcano: clouds may obscure the summit even on a sunny day. Visiting the lake after the market provides a different experience without requiring an added sports activity.

## San Pablo in Ada Tours journeys

On our [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), travellers head from Quito towards Otavalo. The journey includes **a viewpoint overlooking San Pablo Lake and Imbabura Volcano**. The itinerary then continues through Otavalo's market, Cotacachi and Peguche Waterfall.

Do not confuse the advertised panorama stop with a boat excursion. The wider tour combines the Andes, the Amazon and a subsequent Galápagos cruise; here San Pablo is part of an introduction to northern Ecuador's scenery.

Compare other itineraries in our [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) and among [nature journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions about San Pablo Lake

### Where is San Pablo Lake?

In Imbabura Province in northern Ecuador, near Otavalo and at the foot of Imbabura Volcano.

### Can you see the lake without a long hike?

Yes. Views are available from roadside viewpoints, including the Miralago area, without climbing the mountain.

### Are boat trips available?

Water activities are offered around the lake, but their availability, safety arrangements and inclusion in a tour must be confirmed separately.

### What can a visit be combined with?

Otavalo's market and crafts, Peguche Waterfall and other Imbabura Province attractions.

## Which Ecuador tours include views of San Pablo Lake?

[San Pablo Lake](/ecuador/place/san-pablo-lake/) lies in Imbabura Province near [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/). Imbabura Volcano rises above the water, and its slopes can be seen from viewpoints when clouds do not cover the summit. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the lake on the main itinerary.

Both tours feature a stop at [Miralago viewpoint](/ecuador/place/miralago/) on the way to Otavalo. That is where travellers see the lake and volcano. This is **a scenic introduction to San Pablo**, not an included boat excursion, water trek or extended lakeside stay. Keep this difference in mind if you particularly want several hours beside the water.

## Two itineraries: 15 days or 18 days with the Galápagos

| Programme | What follows Imbabura |
|---|---|
| 15 days: Andes and Amazon | Highland reserves, forests and the Amazon |
| 18 days: Ecuador and Galápagos | Mainland nature regions and an island cruise |

On the [15-day "Wildlife of the Andes and Amazon" journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/), San Pablo comes into view on the day's journey from Quito towards Otavalo. That stage also includes local crafts and [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/). The route then continues to high-altitude areas and the Amazon. It suits travellers who want to concentrate on mainland Ecuador's natural areas without a separate cruise.

On the [18-day Ecuador tour with a Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), a panorama of the lake is also part of the day through Miralago and Otavalo market. After the northern Andes, travellers visit other parts of the country before finishing with a Galápagos cruise. The lake is one meaningful stop in a long itinerary; the extra days are largely dedicated to the islands.

Both journeys offer a view of San Pablo, but choosing between them solely for the lake makes little sense: the stop itself is similar. **The main question is whether you want the Galápagos cruise or an extensive mainland Ecuador journey is enough.**

## What you can see from Miralago viewpoint

San Pablo is at the foot of Imbabura, approximately 2,660 m above sea level. Villages and fields surround it, and the lake reflects changing clouds and light. On a clear day, the volcano's wide slopes are visible. With low cloud, the panorama may look very different from a guidebook photograph.

Imbabura Geopark's tourism materials connect the lake with nearby natural and cultural sites, including Peguche. For travellers, the stop offers views of Ecuador's north beyond town streets: broad waters, mountain terrain and hillside settlements.

On the 18-day route, the stop at Miralago comes before Otavalo market, where travellers discover local products. On the 15-day tour, there is also a scenic stop overlooking the lake. Neither of these facts means that boat hire or a separate excursion on the water is necessarily included.

## Combining the lake with Otavalo and nearby attractions

After viewing San Pablo, the day's journey continues to [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/), known for its market and traditional handicrafts. The itinerary also includes [Cotacachi](/ecuador/place/cotacachi/) and [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/). These are separate places within the same northern Andean region: the market provides a cultural experience, the waterfall a walk amid greenery and the lake a broad view of Imbabura.

Their proximity on a map does not mean every tour allocates the same length of time to each stop. Longer programmes have further transfers to make, so a separate extended lakeside walk cannot simply be added without changing the day. If relaxing by the water becomes a priority, the possibility of a separate visit and its conditions need to be agreed when planning the itinerary.

For more options, see [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and the country's [nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). Not every tour that includes Otavalo automatically provides the same San Pablo viewpoint stop.

## Preparing for a stop in the northern Andes

The weather in Imbabura's highlands can change throughout the day. Closed shoes and light protection from wind or rain are useful for a viewpoint stop. Clouds determine how much of the summit is visible, so an unobstructed panorama cannot be guaranteed.

Altitude matters too. A short viewpoint visit normally requires no serious mountaineering preparation, but if you add walks, choose a pace that suits how you feel after previous transfers and days of travel.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through San Pablo Lake

### Is a boat trip on the lake included?

Our programmes provide a view of San Pablo from Miralago viewpoint. A separate boat excursion is not listed among the included services. If this matters, discuss it separately.

### Which tour combines San Pablo with the Galápagos?

The [18-day Ecuador journey with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) starts on the mainland, passes through the northern Andes and later includes an island stage.

### Can you see San Pablo on a trip to Otavalo market?

Yes. On both tours, the lake panorama is part of the journey via [Miralago](/ecuador/place/miralago/) to [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/). The stop's duration is set by the selected itinerary.

### Is the lake suitable for a separate day trip?

Geographically you can visit it independently of a multi-day tour, but this page describes Ada Tours' existing programmes. An independent trip and its services are not automatically part of their price.
